dedupe_keys.name: smart heat and water meter data with building characteristics for single family houses in aalborg aalborg university 34 884 heat meters

description: This dataset holds hourly data from 34,884 commercial smart heat meters and 10,765 commercial smart water meters, covering up to five years (2018 to 2022), mainly from single-family houses in Aalborg Municipality, Denmark, compiled at Aalborg University's Department of the Built Environment. Each building is enriched with up to 86 characteristics from the Danish Building and Dwelling Register (BBR) and Energy Performance Certificate input data, filtered with rule sets to improve quality. The smart meter data were processed with a well-established method into equidistant hourly series without erroneous or missing values. The sources include Aalborg Forsyning, BBR and EPC data. The research portal record, available since 27 November 2023, notes that access to the data is restricted and asks interested researchers to contact the data manager, while the peer-reviewed Data in Brief article describes the dataset and its processing. Coverage is one Danish municipality. Access: restricted, by contacting the data manager; the record was found through the open access article. Caveats: single-family houses only, and file formats were not listed. It suits capacity planning and optimisation studies of district heating demand and water use, and relates to the FunSNM synthetic district heating networks record catalogued here.
